Structural Property: Other structural properties of the FeCoNX/C, CoNX/C, and FeNX/ C, including the morphology, pore structure, and surface composition, were investigated and are compared in Figures S14−S18. It is found that only the surface composition, which correlates with the active site structure, differed among the samples, while the other properties remained similar. Given this, the difference in ORR activity, which will be discussed later, is attributable to the structural difference of the active sites.Further identification of the dual-atom centered site configuration was achieved by performing extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) spectroscopy and EXAFS wavelet transform (WT). In the Fourier transform EXAFS curves, all the CoNX/C, FeNX/C, and FeCoNX/C samples show a prominent peak at ca. 1.5 Å, ascribed to the M−N scattering path. The absence of metallic Co−Co, Fe−Fe, and Fe−Co scattering paths demonstrated that only M−NX coordinates are present in these three catalysts without inactive crystalline phases (Figure 2a,b). WT-EXAFS analysis was further conducted to gain more information pertaining to the coordination environment, as this method can discriminate the backscattering atoms even when they overlap substantially in R-space, by providing not only radial distance resolution but also k-space resolution.
